Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links

Source: R/stat_calc_env_links.R
cli_calc_env_links.Rd

Calculates empirical statistical linkages connecting omics features or network modules with external clinical or environmental indicators. The resulting data frame directly feeds into cliplot_env_network via its links argument. Computes module eigengenes (or centroid abundance profiles), runs bivariate correlation tests (Spearman or Pearson) or Mantel dissimilarity associations, applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) adjustments, and selects statistically significant or top-ranked linkages.

Usage

cli_calc_env_links(
  comm_data,
  env_data,
  modules = NULL,
  method = c("spearman", "pearson"),
  fdr_cutoff = 0.05,
  top_n = 5,
  min_abs_r = 0.2,
  module_summary = c("eigengene", "mean")
)

Arguments

comm_data

Numeric matrix or data frame of omics/microbiome abundance (samples in rows, features in columns).

env_data

Numeric matrix, data frame, or named list of environmental/clinical indicators (samples in rows, indicators in columns). If a named list of 1 to 4 matrices/data frames is supplied, each domain is processed with its domain tag.

modules

Optional named character or factor vector mapping feature IDs to module names (e.g. c("Taxon_1" = "Mod_1", "Taxon_2" = "Mod_1")). If NULL, features are grouped into modules automatically using hierarchical clustering, or individual features are tested directly.

method

Correlation metric: "spearman" (default, robust to outliers) or "pearson".

fdr_cutoff

Numeric significance threshold for Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (default 0.05). If NULL or if no links meet the threshold, the top top_n links are retained.

top_n

Optional integer specifying the maximum number of links to retain per module or environmental domain (default 5).

min_abs_r

Numeric minimum absolute correlation coefficient \(|r|\) required to retain a link (default 0.25).

module_summary

Summary method for features within a module: "eigengene" (first principal component, default) or "mean" (standardized mean abundance).

Value

A data frame containing formatted link linkages with columns:

env

Name of the environmental or clinical indicator variable

module

Name of the target network module

r

Bivariate correlation coefficient

p

Raw asymptotic two-sided p-value

fdr

Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (q-value)

log10p

Negative log10 p-value (\(-\log_{10}(P)\))

sign

Direction of association: "Positive" or "Negative"

domain

Domain name if env_data was supplied as a named list

Examples

set.seed(42)
comm <- matrix(rpois(50 * 30, lambda = 15), nrow = 50, ncol = 30)
colnames(comm) <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:30)
env <- data.frame(
  pH = rnorm(50, 6.5, 0.8),
  Moisture = rnorm(50, 45, 10),
  Temp = rnorm(50, 22, 4)
)
mods <- setNames(paste0("Mod_", rep(1:3, each = 10)), colnames(comm))
links <- cli_calc_env_links(comm, env, modules = mods, method = "spearman")
head(links)
#>    env module          r          p          domain       fdr   log10p     sign
#> 1 Temp  Mod_3 -0.2697239 0.05847339 External_Domain 0.5262605 1.233042 Negative
